name: the Eskeln
identity: Northern herders, bone-carvers and storytellers who measure a winter by how many tales it took to get through.
architecture: Long turf-roofed halls half sunk into the hillside, steaming bathhouses, doorposts carved with family stories, and snow-lanterns along every path.

festivals.name: the Long Telling
festivals.description: The whole hall tells one story together, each person adding a line, for as long as the night lasts.

festivals.name: Sun-Return
festivals.description: Everyone climbs the nearest hill to cheer the first sunrise of the year, loudly, in case it needs encouragement.

festivals.name: the Thaw Market
festivals.description: Sledges full of winter carving race to the coast to trade before the ice goes soft.

values: sharing the warm spot by the fire
pride: Their stories, which are longer than anyone's, and Hjalla Osvik, who is definitely winning the Great Wager.

makersMarks: a knot carved into the haft
a tally of winters notched along the edge
a twist of red wool tied through the pommel

relations.note: The yearly Peak Race, and a long argument over whose horns carry farther.
The Great Wager. Every new letter from Hjalla is read aloud in every hall.
Fellow star-readers; their scholars swap star charts by caravan.
